correctness.rationale: The original SLOGAN.txt wrongly excludes equality, and the frozen proof does not explicitly establish the area-halving assertion or justify the below-threshold argument without assuming injectivity. The complete replacements RESULT.md and SLOGAN.txt under /workspace/repairs/4/ retain the theorem, correct the endpoint wording, and supply those arguments. In the rotating frame the velocity is (-r,H), H=h+h'', so it is regular and has tangent index 1. Its determinant with acceleration is r(r-H')+H^2. Positive weights give H'<=R_n; the first cosine fixes all simultaneous maximizing phases, and odd beta aligns all the higher cosines there with H=0. At and above the threshold the tangent angle strictly increases through 2pi even with isolated zero curvature. Every normal has a unique maximizing parameter, and every curve point maximizes projection in its oriented outward normal direction. This gives injectivity and identifies the image with the strictly convex boundary of its convex hull. Below the threshold the determinant has opposite signs at pi/beta and 0. A regular curve whose image is a convex boundary has a supporting tangent at each parameter; an interior point stays on a fixed oriented side along the whole parameter circle. The second derivative of the signed distance numerator to any such tangent must then have that weak sign, contradicting the two witnesses without a prior injectivity assumption. For halving, the derivative of the signed area enclosed by the arc and closing chord is half the determinant of the chord with the sum of endpoint velocities. Both are parallel to u', so the area is constant; the pi shift gives the complementary area. Taylor expansion gives coefficient (R_n+S_n/2)/R_n^2, and the geometric sums give the stated growth in the original parameter regime. The prior independent symbolic determinant, coefficient and sample radii replay remains applicable: python3 /workspace/review_replay.py, check 4. Finite diagnostics do not establish global convexity.
